blocks.passage:
The most common mistake in problem solving is rushing to the solution before understanding the problem. We see a symptom, grab the first explanation that feels right, and start fixing — only to discover, weeks later, that the real cause was somewhere else entirely.

A useful discipline is five whys: ask "why?" five times in a row, going deeper each time. The surface problem is rarely the real one. A late delivery might be due to a missed container, which was due to a supplier change, which was due to a sourcing decision taken six months ago for an entirely different reason.

Root causes are almost always less dramatic and more systemic than the symptom suggests. Good problem solvers stay patient, resist blame, and look for the quiet structural issues that allowed the visible problem to happen in the first place.

audio.text:
So the monthly report has been late three times in a row. The easy answer is "the analyst is slow" — but let's not stop there. Let's ask why.

Why was it late? Because the data arrived late. Why did the data arrive late? Because the sales figures weren't ready. Why weren't they ready? Because the regional numbers come in on the last working day, which is exactly when the report is due.

So the real problem isn't the analyst at all. It's the schedule. The report deadline and the data deadline are the same day, which is impossible by design.

The quick fix would be to push the analyst to work late — but that just hides the issue until next month. The proper fix is to move the report deadline two days later, or bring the data in earlier. Either way, it's a process change, not a people problem.

Let's write it up as a scheduling root cause, not blame anyone, and propose the deadline change to the team.

items.q: The **root cause** of a problem is…
items.why: Root cause = causa raiz, a razão de fundo.

items.q: A **symptom** is…
options: the visible sign of a deeper problem
items.why: Symptom = sintoma, o sinal visível.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "That's only a **quick fix** — it ___ the real issue."
items.why: Quick fix = solução rápida, que costuma esconder o problema de fundo.

items.q: "It's a **systemic** issue." Systemic means…
options: built into the way the system works
items.why: Systemic = sistêmico, próprio da estrutura.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "Let's not ___ the analyst — the schedule is the problem."
items.why: To blame = culpar.

items.q: "Let's **get to the bottom of** why it's late." To get to the bottom of means to…
items.why: Get to the bottom of = chegar à causa real.

items.q: "That doesn't **add up** — the numbers don't match." To add up means to…
items.why: Add up = fazer sentido, bater.

items.q: "We keep **papering over the cracks** instead of fixing it." To paper over the cracks means to…
items.why: Paper over the cracks = disfarçar o problema sem resolvê-lo.

items.q: "Let's **dig into** the process before blaming anyone." To dig into means to…
items.why: Dig into = investigar a fundo.

items.q: "The late data is what's **holding up** the report." To hold something up means to…
items.why: Hold up = atrasar, travar.
